classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that an acute angle with equal sine and cosine is 45°, using exact ratios or the complementary-angle relationship, then obtain the other acute angle from the right-triangle angle sum.

content.prompt: Find $\angle BAC$ and $\angle BCA$ if $\sin A=\cos A$.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with A upper left, B lower left and C lower right; right angle at B.
spec.mathematics: AB vertical, BC horizontal, AC the hypotenuse. No additional side or angle annotations.

answer.worked:
Since $A$ is acute, use $\cos A=\sin(90^\circ-A)$.
$$\begin{align*}\sin A&=\sin(90^\circ-A)\\A&=90^\circ-A\\2A&=90^\circ\\\angle BAC&=45^\circ\\\angle BCA&=90^\circ-45^\circ\\\angle BCA&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$
